proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(g_a(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}\).  First consider any admissible two-sign late-void residual pair \(\widetilde r^+=g\), \(\widetilde r^-=-g\), where \(g=0\) on \([0,a]\), \(|g(u)|\le M\), and \(g\) is \(L_r\)-Lipschitz.  For \(u>a\), the Lipschitz condition and \(g(a)=0\) give
\[
 |g(u)|=|g(u)-g(a)|\le L_r(u-a).
\]
Combining this inequality with the outcome bound yields
\[
 |g(u)|\le g_a(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}.
\]
The capped clipped ramp attains equality pointwise.  Hence every such witness has limiting two-sign causal separation at most
\[
 2\int_0^1 |g(u)|\,du
 \le 2\int_0^{1-a}\min\{L_rs,M\}\,ds
 =:d(1-a),
\]
and the clipped ramp attains the last expression.  Direct integration gives
\[
 d(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L_rx^2,&L_rx\le M,\\
 2Mx-M^2/L_r,&L_rx>M.
 \end{cases}
\]
Thus \(d\) is continuous and strictly increasing on \([0,1]\), and
\[
 d(1)=
 \begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\le M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M,
 \end{cases}
 =d_{\max}.
\]
If \(L_r\le M\), then \(d_{\max}=L_r\le M^2/L_r\), so every \(d<d_{\max}\) is on the quadratic branch.  If \(L_r>M\), the clipping point \(x=M/L_r\) belongs to \((0,1)\) and has image \(M^2/L_r\).  Solving \(d=d(x)\) on the two branches gives exactly the displayed \(x(d)\).  Consequently
\[
 0<x(d)<1,\qquad a(d)=1-x(d)\in(0,1),
 \qquad d(x(d))=d.
\]
This also proves that the residual elbow is interior exactly when \(L_r>M\).

Fix \(d\in(0,d_{\max})\) and choose the capped clipped-ramp pair with start \(a_\star=a(d)\).  The capped-ramp membership proposition places both signs in the declared structured class.  With
\[
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\},
\]
uniform asymptotic honesty therefore implies
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\le\alpha.
\]
The sharp two-sign clipped-ramp theorem supplies
\[
 \Delta_n\ge d(1-a(d))=d,
 \qquad \eta_n\longrightarrow a(d)^c,
\]
and, under either sign,
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 \ge[\eta_n-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
Because \(\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}\subseteq
\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}\), continuity and monotonicity of \(z\mapsto[z]_+\) give
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge[a(d)^c-2\alpha]_+
 =[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]

For completeness, the attaining allocation can be read directly from the common void component.  Outside the void event, the first nonzero treated outcome identifies the sign, so report the corresponding true singleton.  On the void, if \(\eta_n>2\alpha\), give unconditional void masses \(\alpha\), \(\alpha\), and \(\eta_n-2\alpha\) to the positive singleton, the negative singleton, and the two-target set.  If \(\alpha<\eta_n\le2\alpha\), give unconditional void masses \(\eta_n-\alpha\), \(\eta_n-\alpha\), and \(2\alpha-\eta_n\) to the two singletons and the empty set.  If \(\eta_n\le\alpha\), report the empty set on the void.  Each sign then has miscoverage at most \(\alpha\), and the only output of positive diameter is the two-target set, whose diameter is \(\Delta_n\ge d\).  Hence
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 = [\eta_n-2\alpha]_+
 \longrightarrow[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]
This is attainment only inside the selected pair.

Finally, suppose another admissible late-void residual pair starts at \(a'=1-x'\) and has limiting separation at least \(d\).  The pointwise envelope already proved implies \(d\le d(x')\).  Strict monotonicity of \(d\) gives \(x'\ge x(d)\), whence
\[
 (a')^c=(1-x')^c\le(1-x(d))^c.
\]
This certifies optimality within the stated constant-intensity late-void witness geometry.

For the exact diagnostic, set \(c=a_\star=1/2\), \(L_r=1/2\), \(M\ge1/4\), and \(\alpha=0.05\).  Then the clipped residual is the original linear ramp and
\[
 d(1/2)=\frac18,
 \qquad
 [(1/2)^{1/2}-0.1]_+
 =0.6071067811865475\ldots.
\]
With \(m_n=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), exact enumeration at the four smallest horizons gives
\[
 (\Delta_1,\Delta_2,\Delta_3,\Delta_4)
 =\left(\frac12,\frac14,\frac29,\frac3{16}\right)
\]
and
\[
 (\eta_1,\eta_2,\eta_3,\eta_4)
 =\left(\frac12,\frac34,\frac58,\frac{35}{48}\right).
\]
Every enumerated separation exceeds \(1/8\), and each void mass is exactly the product used in the common-subprobability proof.
Thus the result preserves the exact \(1/8\) and \(0.60710678\) obstruction.  It does not alter the separate positive calibration theorem, the directed \(13/32\) certificate, or the high-hazard \(0.442M\) result.

The sourced baseline-class lemma records that Li and Zhao allow fixed finite-population potential outcomes, strictly positive history-measurable treatment probabilities summing to one, and history-measurable AIPW regressions.  In the capped clipped-ramp construction,
\[
 e_{nt}(1)=\min\{\rho,c/t\},
 \qquad e_{nt}(0)=1-e_{nt}(1).
\]
These probabilities are deterministic, strictly between zero and one, and sum to one.  The capped-ramp membership proposition supplies fixed bounded outcomes and the predictable zero regression.  Thus every capped clipped-ramp array belongs to the published baseline binary adaptive class.

It remains to verify the negligible-increment obstruction rather than assume it.  Put
\[
 g(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a_\star)_+,M\},
 \qquad
 X_{nt}=(A_{nt}-e_{nt})\frac{\sigma g(t/n)}{e_{nt}}.
\]
Predictable randomization gives
\[
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=0
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})
 =g(t/n)^2\{e_{nt}^{-1}-1\}.
\]
If \(s<t\), then \(X_{ns}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,t-1}\)-measurable, so iterated conditioning gives \(\mathbb E(X_{ns}X_{nt})=0\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), the propensity cap is inactive whenever \(g(t/n)>0\).  Therefore the variance \(W_n\) of the \(\sqrt n\)-scaled scalar AIPW error is
\[
 W_n=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n g(t/n)^2(t/c-1),
\]
and right-Riemann convergence yields
\[
 \frac{W_n}{n}\longrightarrow
 w_\star:=\frac1c\int_{a_\star}^1u g(u)^2\,du>0.
\]
At \(t=n\), \(g(1)=\min\{L_r(1-a_\star),M\}>0\), the regression envelope is zero, and the smaller binary assignment probability is \(c/n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Hence the scalar negligible-maximum ratio in the sourced Condition 3(ii) obeys
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 W_n^{-1}n^{-1}
 \max_{1\le t\le n}
 \frac{(L_t+M_t)^2}{\underline e_t^2}
 \ge \frac{g(1)^2}{c^2w_\star}>0.
\]
It is not \(o(1)\).  At the unprojected two-arm level the control contribution is identically zero, so the full covariance also has a zero control row and column; this is consistent with, rather than a repair of, the same Gaussian-premise failure.

Uniform honesty over Li and Zhao's baseline class implies honesty on each capped two-sign subclass.  Applying the already proved optimized constant-intensity frontier gives the displayed lower bound.  This inclusion argument constructs no confidence procedure on the larger class and therefore transfers neither pairwise attainment nor the structured positive calibration theorem.

added_lemmas.statement: Every intensity-optimized clipped-ramp array has fixed potential outcomes bounded by \(M\), deterministic predictable assignment probabilities in \((0,\rho]\), and predictable zero regressions.  Its profiles satisfy \(\bar q_\star\in\mathcal Q\) and \(r^\sigma\in\mathcal R\), and \(r_{nt}(1)=r^\sigma(t/n)\) exactly.  For all sufficiently large \(n\), the propensity cap is inactive simultaneously for every \(t\ge\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\) and every \(t>\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor\); the early rare-arm term and its predictable quadratic variation are zero, and \(G_n=\Omega\).  This is an eventual profile-contract conclusion only: the construction is not asserted to satisfy \(\Pr(G_n)\ge1-\kappa_n\) for every finite \(n\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The potential outcomes and regressions are deterministic arrays, so they are fixed under assignment.  By construction,
\[
 |Y_{nt}^\sigma(1)|=g_{a_\star}(t/n)\le M,
 \qquad Y_{nt}^\sigma(0)=0,
\]
and the outcome bound follows.  Since \(c/2\le\bar q_\star(u)\le c\) and \(t\ge1\),
\[
 0<e_{nt}=\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\}\le\rho<1.
\]
The probabilities are deterministic and hence predictable, and the declared conditional Bernoulli law is a valid adaptive assignment law.  The zero regression is predictable and obeys its bound.

At \(u=0\), \(\bar q_\star(0)=c\).  Also
\[
 c/2\le\bar q_\star(u)\le c\le K.
\]
The functions \(u\mapsto c-L_qu\) and \(u\mapsto c/2\) are respectively \(L_q\)-Lipschitz and constant.  The elementary inequality
\[
 |\max\{x_1,x_2\}-\max\{y_1,y_2\}|
 \le\max\{|x_1-y_1|,|x_2-y_2|\}
\]
therefore shows that \(\bar q_\star\) is \(L_q\)-Lipschitz.  These three facts prove \(\bar q_\star\in\mathcal Q\).  Similarly,
\[
 |r^\sigma(u)|=g_{a_\star}(u)\le M\le B,
\]
and truncating the \(L_r\)-Lipschitz function \(L_r(u-a_\star)_+\) at \(M\) preserves its Lipschitz modulus.  Thus \(r^\sigma\in\mathcal R\).  Because the regression is zero,
\[
 r_{nt}(1)=Y_{nt}^\sigma(1)-m_{nt}(1)=r^\sigma(t/n)
\]
for every \(n,t\).

The conditions \(n\varepsilon_n\to\infty\), \(a_\star>0\), and \(\bar q_\star\le c\) imply that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \frac{\bar q_\star(t/n)}t\le\frac ct<\rho
\]
both whenever \(t\ge\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\) and whenever \(t>\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor\).  Thus the cap is inactive on both ranges.  On the first range,
\[
 te_{nt}=\bar q_\star(t/n),
\]
so the intensity discrepancy in \(G_n\) is zero, while the residual discrepancy is already zero for every \(n\).

Finally, \(\varepsilon_n+1/n\to0<a_\star\).  Hence eventually every \(t<\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\) satisfies
\[
 t/n<\varepsilon_n+1/n<a_\star,
\]
and therefore \(r_{nt}(1)=0\).  Each summand of the early rare-arm martingale is zero, so both that martingale and its predictable quadratic variation equal zero.  All three clauses defining \(G_n\) then hold identically, proving \(G_n=\Omega\) for sufficiently large \(n\).  No step proves the corresponding assertion at the exceptional finite prefixes, which is why no all-horizon profile-contract membership is claimed.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix an intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair and define
\[
 m_n=\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor,
 \qquad
 V_n=\bigcap_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\{A_{nt}=0\},
 \qquad
 \eta_n^\star=\prod_{t=m_n+1}^{n}
 \left[1-\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\}\right],
\]
and
\[
 \Delta_n^\star=\tau_n^+-\tau_n^-
 =\frac2n\sum_{t=1}^{n}\min\{L_r(t/n-a_\star)_+,M\}.
\]
For every possibly randomized complete-log confidence set \(D_n=D_n(O_n,U)\), where \(U\) is independent of the experiment and identically distributed under both signs, let
\[
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\}.
\]
With \([z]_+=\max\{z,0\}\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(\varnothing)=0\), for every \(n\) and either sign,
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n^\star\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
For each \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the inequality is attained within this two-sign subexperiment by a possibly randomized complete-log confidence set of maximum miscoverage at most \(\alpha\), for which
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n^\star\}
 =[\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+.
\]
Writing \(x=1-a_\star\), one has
\[
 \Delta_n^\star\ge d(x),\qquad
 \Delta_n^\star\longrightarrow d(x),
\]
where
\[
 d(x)=2\int_0^x\min\{L_rs,M\}\,ds
 =\begin{cases}
 L_rx^2,&L_rx\le M,\\
 2Mx-M^2/L_r,&L_rx>M.
 \end{cases}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \eta_n^\star\longrightarrow\omega(a_\star)
 :=\exp\{-H(a_\star)\},
 \qquad
 H(a)=\int_a^1\frac{\bar q_\star(u)}u\,du.
\]
If \(0\le L_q\le c/2\), then
\[
 H(a)=c\log(1/a)-L_q(1-a).
\]
If \(L_q>c/2\) and \(u_q=c/(2L_q)\), then
\[
 H(a)=
 \begin{cases}
 (c/2)\log(1/a),&a\ge u_q,\\
 c\log(u_q/a)-L_q(u_q-a)+(c/2)\log(1/u_q),&a<u_q.
 \end{cases}
\]
Finally, every \(q'\in\mathcal Q\) satisfies
\[
 q'(u)\ge\bar q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\},
\]
so, for every fixed start and every \(n\), \(\bar q_\star\) maximizes the common late-void product among deterministic designs \(e_{nt}^{q'}=\min\{\rho,q'(t/n)/t\}\).  All attainment assertions are confined to the displayed two-sign pair.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(g_a(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}\).  The construction gives
\[
 \tau_n^\sigma=\frac{\sigma}{n}\sum_{t=1}^n g_{a_\star}(t/n),
\]
and subtraction proves the formula for \(\Delta_n^\star\).  The function \(g_{a_\star}\) is nondecreasing.  On each interval \(((t-1)/n,t/n]\),
\[
 g_{a_\star}(u)\le g_{a_\star}(t/n),
\]
so the right-Riemann sum satisfies
\[
 \Delta_n^\star
 \ge2\int_0^1g_{a_\star}(u)\,du
 =2\int_0^{1-a_\star}\min\{L_rs,M\}\,ds
 =d(1-a_\star).
\]
Because \(g_{a_\star}\) is continuous, the same right-Riemann sums converge to the integral.  Splitting the integral at \(s=M/L_r\), when this point lies below \(x\), gives the two displayed branches of \(d(x)\).

Let \(V_{n,s}=\bigcap_{t=m_n+1}^{s}\{A_{nt}=0\}\).  This event is \(\mathcal F_{n,s}\)-measurable.  Predictable randomization and the deterministic propensity imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Pr_\sigma(V_{n,s})
 &=\mathbb E_\sigma\!\left[
 \mathbf 1_{V_{n,s-1}}
 \Pr_\sigma(A_{ns}=0\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1})
 \right]\\
 &=\left[1-\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(s/n)/s\}\right]
 \Pr_\sigma(V_{n,s-1}).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Iteration proves \(\Pr_\sigma(V_n)=\eta_n^\star\) under both signs.  Every factor is positive because the treatment propensity is at most \(\rho<1\).

For the limit, \(m_n/n\to a_\star>0\).  Thus the cap is inactive throughout \(t>m_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Put \(p_{nt}=\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\) on this range.  Since \(p_{nt}\le c/t\),
\[
 \max_{t>m_n}p_{nt}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{t=m_n+1}^n p_{nt}^2
 \le c^2\sum_{t=m_n+1}^n t^{-2}longrightarrow0.
\]
For \(0\le z<1\), integration of \(z/(1-z)\) gives
\[
 0\le-\log(1-z)-z\le\frac{z^2}{2(1-z)}.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \log\eta_n^\star
 =-\sum_{t=m_n+1}^n\frac{\bar q_\star(t/n)}t+o(1).
\]
The function \(u\mapsto\bar q_\star(u)/u\) is continuous on the compact interval \([a_\star/2,1]\).  Hence
\[
 \sum_{t=m_n+1}^n\frac{\bar q_\star(t/n)}t
 =\frac1n\sum_{t=m_n+1}^n
 \frac{\bar q_\star(t/n)}{t/n}
 \longrightarrow\int_{a_\star}^1\frac{\bar q_\star(u)}u\,du
 =H(a_\star).
\]
Exponentiating proves \(\eta_n^\star\to e^{-H(a_\star)}\).

If \(0\le L_q\le c/2\), then \(c-L_qu\ge c/2\) throughout \([0,1]\), so \(\bar q_\star(u)=c-L_qu\) and
\[
 H(a)=\int_a^1(c/u-L_q)\,du
 =c\log(1/a)-L_q(1-a).
\]
If \(L_q>c/2\), the affine branch meets the floor at \(u_q=c/(2L_q)\in(0,1)\).  When \(a\ge u_q\), direct integration of \((c/2)/u\) gives the first split formula.  When \(a<u_q\), splitting at \(u_q\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 H(a)
 &=\int_a^{u_q}(c/u-L_q)\,du
   +\int_{u_q}^1\frac{c}{2u}\,du\\
 &=c\log(u_q/a)-L_q(u_q-a)
   +(c/2)\log(1/u_q),
 \end{aligned}
\]
as asserted.

We next prove the information inequality.  The assignment law is identical under both signs.  For \(t\le m_n\), one has \(t/n\le a_\star\), so both treated potential outcomes are zero.  On \(V_n\), every later unit is assigned control and also has observed outcome zero.  The propensity and regression logs are deterministic and identical.  Therefore, for every measurable set \(E\),
\[
 \Pr_+\{(O_n,U)\in E,V_n\}
 =\Pr_-\{(O_n,U)\in E,V_n\}
 =:\nu_n(E),
\]
where \(\nu_n\) is a common subprobability measure of mass \(\eta_n^\star\), dominated by both sign-specific laws.  If \(E_{\sigma,n}=\{\tau_n^\sigma\in D_n\}\), then
\[
 \nu_n(E_{\sigma,n}^c)
 \le\Pr_\sigma(E_{\sigma,n}^c)
 \le\gamma_n.
\]
The union bound for the finite measure \(\nu_n\) yields
\[
 \nu_n(E_{+,n}\cap E_{-,n})
 \ge\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n.
\]
On this intersection the reported set contains both causal targets, separated by \(\Delta_n^\star\).  Domination by either experimental law and nonnegativity of probabilities prove
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n^\star\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]

For attainment, take an independent \(U\sim\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\).  On \(V_n^c\), the first treated unit after \(m_n\) has a nonzero observed outcome whose sign equals \(\sigma\); report the corresponding true singleton.  On \(V_n\), if \(\eta_n^\star>2\alpha\), allocate conditional probabilities
\[
 \frac{\alpha}{\eta_n^\star},\quad
 \frac{\alpha}{\eta_n^\star},\quad
 1-\frac{2\alpha}{\eta_n^\star}
\]
to \(\{\tau_n^+\}\), \(\{\tau_n^-\}\), and \(\{\tau_n^+,\tau_n^-\}\), respectively.  If \(\alpha<\eta_n^\star\le2\alpha\), allocate
\[
 \frac{\eta_n^\star-\alpha}{\eta_n^\star},\quad
 \frac{\eta_n^\star-\alpha}{\eta_n^\star},\quad
 \frac{2\alpha-\eta_n^\star}{\eta_n^\star}
\]
to the two singletons and the empty set.  If \(\eta_n^\star\le\alpha\), report the empty set on \(V_n\).  The displayed probabilities are nonnegative and sum to one in their respective cases.  Adding the certain coverage on \(V_n^c\) shows that each sign has miscoverage at most \(\alpha\).  The two-target set is the only output of positive diameter, and its unconditional probability is exactly \([\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+\).  This proves pairwise sharpness.

Finally, take any \(q'\in\mathcal Q\).  Its anchor and Lipschitz condition imply
\[
 q'(u)\ge q'(0)-L_qu=c-L_qu,
\]
while its lower bound gives \(q'(u)\ge c/2\).  Hence \(q'(u)\ge\bar q_\star(u)\) pointwise.  Since \(z\mapsto\min\{\rho,z/t\}\) is nondecreasing and \(z\mapsto1-z\) is nonincreasing,
\[
 \prod_{t=m_n+1}^n
 \left[1-\min\{\rho,q'(t/n)/t\}\right]
 \le\eta_n^\star.
\]
Thus \(\bar q_\star\) is pointwise admissible and maximizes the finite common late-void mass for every fixed start.  When \(L_q=0\), it equals the constant profile \(c\), so the pre-existing constant-intensity theorem and its exact small-horizon diagnostic are recovered without alteration.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(L_r>0\), and define
\[
 d_{\max}=\begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\le M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M,
 \end{cases}
\]
\[
 x(d)=\begin{cases}
 \sqrt{d/L_r},&d\le M^2/L_r,\\
 \{d+M^2/L_r\}/(2M),&d>M^2/L_r,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad a(d)=1-x(d),
\]
and
\[
 H(a)=\int_a^1\frac{\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}}u\,du.
\]
For any \(0<d<d_{\max}\), select the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair with start \(a(d)\), and put
\[
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\}.
\]
If \(\limsup_n\gamma_n\le\alpha\), then, under each sign,
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+.
\]
This bound is attained asymptotically by the exact randomized allocation inside the selected two-sign pair.  Jointly over deterministic intensity profiles in \(\mathcal Q\) and late-void two-sign residual witnesses that vanish on \([0,a]\), are bounded by \(M\), and have Lipschitz modulus at most \(L_r\), the displayed expression is the optimized late-void envelope at diameter \(d\).

The residual elbow is \(d_r=M^2/L_r\) and is interior exactly when \(L_r>M\).  When \(L_q>c/2\), put \(u_q=c/(2L_q)\); the additional intensity elbow is
\[
 d_q=d(1-u_q)=d\!\left(1-\frac{c}{2L_q}\right).
\]
When both elbows are interior, either ordering \(d_q<d_r\) or \(d_r<d_q\) is possible.  The function \(H\) has the explicit forms
\[
 H(a)=c\log(1/a)-L_q(1-a),\qquad 0\le L_q\le c/2,
\]
and, for \(L_q>c/2\),
\[
 H(a)=
 \begin{cases}
 (c/2)\log(1/a),&a\ge u_q,\\
 c\log(u_q/a)-L_q(u_q-a)+(c/2)\log(1/u_q),&a<u_q.
 \end{cases}
\]
No full-structured-class honesty premise or global minimax attainment is claimed for this joint-intensity result.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The right-Riemann calculation in the sharp joint-pair theorem gives the continuous strictly increasing separation map
\[
 d(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L_rx^2,&L_rx\le M,\\
 2Mx-M^2/L_r,&L_rx>M.
 \end{cases}
\]
Its endpoint value is \(d_{\max}\).  Solving \(d=d(x)\) on each branch proves the displayed inverse \(x(d)\), and for \(0<d<d_{\max}\),
\[
 x(d)\in(0,1),\qquad a(d)=1-x(d)\in(0,1),
 \qquad d(x(d))=d.
\]

Fix this selected pair.  The finite common-subprobability inequality gives
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n^\star\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+,
\]
while the same theorem gives
\[
 \Delta_n^\star\ge d(x(d))=d,
 \qquad
 \eta_n^\star\longrightarrow\exp\{-H(a(d))\}.
\]
Thus
\[
 \{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n^\star\}
 \subseteq\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}.
\]
Using \(\limsup_n\gamma_n\le\alpha\) and continuity of the positive-part map yields
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge[\exp\{-H(a(d))\}-2\alpha]_+,
\]
which is the stated formula because \(a(d)=1-x(d)\).  The randomized allocation from the sharp theorem has miscoverage at most \(\alpha\) and selects its only positive-diameter output with probability \([\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+\).  Since that output has diameter \(\Delta_n^\star\ge d\), its probability converges to the lower envelope.  This proves attainment within the selected pair only.

We now certify joint optimality of the witness.  If an admissible late-void residual pair starts at \(a'=1-x'\) and has limiting causal separation at least \(d\), boundedness and Lipschitz continuity imply pointwise
\[
 |g(u)|\le\min\{L_r(u-a')_+,M\}.
\]
Consequently its limiting separation is at most \(d(x')\).  Since \(d\) is strictly increasing,
\[
 d\le d(x')\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x'\ge x(d)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a'\le a(d).
\]
For fixed \(a'\), pointwise minimality of \(\bar q_\star\) in \(\mathcal Q\) shows that no other deterministic admissible intensity has a larger late-void probability.  Moreover, because \(\bar q_\star(u)>0\),
\[
 H(a_1)-H(a_2)=\int_{a_1}^{a_2}\frac{\bar q_\star(u)}u\,du>0
 \quad\text{whenever }0<a_1<a_2<1.
\]
Thus \(\omega(a)=e^{-H(a)}\) is strictly increasing in \(a\), and
\[
 \omega(a')\le\omega(a(d)).
\]
The clipped residual at \(a(d)\) and \(\bar q_\star\) attain both inequalities, establishing the joint late-void certificate.

The residual formula changes branch when \(x=M/L_r\), whose image is \(d_r=M^2/L_r\); this point lies in \((0,1)\) exactly when \(L_r>M\).  If \(L_q>c/2\), the intensity changes branch at \(a=u_q=c/(2L_q)\).  Since \(a=1-x\), its image on the diameter scale is \(d_q=d(1-u_q)\).  There is no forced ordering.  For example, with \(c=M=1\), \(L_r=2\), and \(L_q=3/5\),
\[
 1-u_q=\frac16<\frac{M}{L_r}=\frac12,
\]
so \(d_q<d_r\).  With \(c=M=1\), \(L_r=4\), and \(L_q=1\),
\[
 \frac{M}{L_r}=\frac14<1-u_q=\frac12,
\]
so \(d_r<d_q\).  The explicit formulas for \(H\) were derived by direct integration in the sharp joint-pair theorem.  None of these arguments uses all-horizon membership in the structured profile-contract class.

added_lemmas.statement:
Every intensity-optimized clipped-ramp array belongs, for every \(n\), to Li and Zhao's baseline binary finite-population adaptive-design class.  Its nonzero treated projection retains nonnegligible late rare-arm increments and therefore fails the negligible-increment requirement in their Gaussian Condition 3(ii).  Define
\[
 d_{\max}=\begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\le M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M,
 \end{cases}
\]
and, for \(0<d<d_{\max}\),
\[
 x(d)=\begin{cases}
 \sqrt{d/L_r},&d\le M^2/L_r,\\
 \{d+M^2/L_r\}/(2M),&d>M^2/L_r.
 \end{cases}
\]
Also define
\[
 H(a)=\int_a^1\frac{\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}}u\,du
\]
for \(a\in(0,1)\).  If a sequence of possibly randomized complete-log confidence sets is asymptotically \((1-\alpha)\)-honest uniformly over Li and Zhao's baseline binary class, then for every \(0<d<d_{\max}\), under each sign of the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair with start \(1-x(d)\),
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+.
\]
Only this converse transfers.  Neither the pair-specific attaining allocation nor the positive profile-net calibration theorem is asserted on Li and Zhao's larger class.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For every \(n,t\), define the two binary assignment probabilities by
\[
 e_{nt}(1)=\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\},
 \qquad e_{nt}(0)=1-e_{nt}(1).
\]
The joint-family properties proposition proves that both are strictly positive, deterministic functions of every history, and sum to one.  It also proves that the potential outcomes are fixed and bounded and that the zero regression is predictable.  The sourced baseline-class lemma therefore places every finite array in Li and Zhao's baseline binary adaptive class.  This conclusion does not use the all-horizon profile contract.

Let \(a\in(0,1)\) and \(g_a(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}\).  For the treated scalar projection define
\[
 X_{nt}=(A_{nt}-e_{nt})\frac{\sigma g_a(t/n)}{e_{nt}}.
\]
Predictable randomization gives
\[
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})
 =g_a(t/n)^2\{e_{nt}^{-1}-1\}.
\]
The increments are pairwise orthogonal by iterated conditioning.  The cap is inactive for every \(t>\lfloor an\rfloor\) when \(n\) is sufficiently large.  If \(W_n\) denotes the variance of the \(\sqrt n\)-scaled scalar AIPW error, then
\[
 W_n=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n
 g_a(t/n)^2\left\{\frac{t}{\bar q_\star(t/n)}-1\right\}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), and Riemann convergence gives
\[
 \frac{W_n}{n}\longrightarrow
 w_\star(a):=\int_a^1\frac{u g_a(u)^2}{\bar q_\star(u)}\,du>0.
\]
At \(t=n\), the outcome envelope is at least
\[
 g_a(1)=\min\{L_r(1-a),M\}>0,
\]
the regression envelope is zero, and the smaller binary assignment probability is \(\bar q_\star(1)/n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Thus the negligible-maximum ratio recorded in the sourced Condition 3(ii) has lower limit at least
\[
 \frac{g_a(1)^2}{\bar q_\star(1)^2w_\star(a)}>0.
\]
It cannot be \(o(1)\).  This establishes the late-increment obstruction directly; it does not assume a Gaussian limit.

Now fix \(0<d<d_{\max}\) and set \(a=1-x(d)\).  Uniform baseline-class honesty and the just-proved every-\(n\) inclusion imply
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \gamma_n
 =\limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\}
 \le\alpha.
\]
Apply the finite common-subprobability inequality for this selected pair:
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n^\star\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
The same finite calculation gives \(\Delta_n^\star\ge d(x(d))=d\), and the void-product calculation gives
\[
 \eta_n^\star\longrightarrow\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}.
\]
Taking lower limits proves the displayed converse.  The argument uses baseline honesty only to obtain pair honesty and then uses the exact two-law common component; it invokes neither structured-class honesty nor any positive calibration result.  The attaining allocation knows the selected pair, so it does not transfer to the larger baseline class.

proposed.construction:
Fix \(c>0\), \(\rho\in(0,1)\), \(a_\star\in(0,1)\), \(M>0\), \(L_r>0\), \(L_q\ge0\), and \(K\ge c\).  Define
\[
 \bar q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\},
 \qquad
 g_{a_\star}(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a_\star)_+,M\}.
\]
For \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), put
\[
 r^\sigma(u)=\sigma g_{a_\star}(u),\qquad
 e_{nt}=\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\},
\]
and set
\[
 m_{nt}(0)=m_{nt}(1)=0,qquad
 Y_{nt}^\sigma(0)=0,qquad
 Y_{nt}^\sigma(1)=r^\sigma(t/n).
\]
The sequential randomization law is
\(\Pr_\sigma(A_{nt}=1\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=e_{nt}\), and the complete observation is \(O_n=(A_{n1:n},e_{n1:n},Y_{n1:n}^{\mathrm{obs}},m_{n1:n})\).

prose_updates.tldr: At the critical rare-arm boundary, the finite-population AIPW error need not be Gaussian. On this note's structured binary profile subclass, a stopped adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson transfer and directed-rational convolution give a computable atom-safe confidence interval with uniform randomization coverage and explicit oracle slack. Separately, the existing constant-intensity capped clipped-ramp theorem remains the structured-class residual-optimized converse. A new pair-honesty result also optimizes intensity: \(\bar q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) is pointwise minimal in \(\mathcal Q\), yielding the joint envelope \( [\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha]_+ \) and a second intensity elbow. Exact attainment is only within each selected two-sign pair. Li and Zhao baseline-class honesty inherits both converse forms by separate subclass arguments, but neither positive calibration nor attainment. The exact \(1/8\), \(0.60710678\) diagnostic, directed \(13/32\) certificate, and high-hazard \(0.442M\) radius remain unchanged.

project_justification.gap: Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive-design class permits positive history-dependent assignment probabilities, but their Gaussian AIPW theorem requires a negligible-maximum condition that fails at bounded cumulative hazard. Existing adaptive and i.i.d. width results neither calibrate the signed atomic compound-Poisson law nor jointly optimize the complete-log common-void obstruction over the anchored Lipschitz intensity class and the bounded Lipschitz residual class.

For all-estimator information limits, clipped residuals saturate \(\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}\), while the pointwise-minimal intensity \(\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) maximizes late-void mass and creates an additional profile elbow.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the finite adaptive-to-Poisson transfer and profile-net interval theorem on the declared structured subclass, preserves the exact constant-intensity clipped-ramp frontier, and adds a joint intensity-residual frontier under honesty on each selected two-sign pair. A direct sourced inclusion argument transfers only the joint converse to Li and Zhao's baseline binary class. Pairwise attainment, positive calibration, the exact ramp certificate, and the high-hazard radius retain their separately stated scopes.

prose_updates.related_work: Li and Zhao (2026) provide the closest design-based setup: fixed finite-population potential outcomes, positive assignment probabilities that may be prespecified functions of history, and predictable AIPW regression. Their baseline binary class contains both the constant-intensity and intensity-optimized clipped ramps at every finite horizon, but their Theorem 4(ii) assumes Condition 3; these bounded-hazard witnesses fail its negligible-maximum part because late standardized increments remain nonnegligible. The constant-intensity converse transfers by its original subclass argument. The joint-intensity converse transfers directly from baseline-class honesty to pair honesty and then through the exact common-void inequality; it does not rely on all-horizon membership in this note's profile-contract class. Matching confidence-set constructions remain sharp only inside selected two-sign experiments, and the positive profile-net theorem remains confined to this note's structured subclass. Bibaut and Kallus (2025) organize adaptive inference into Gaussian repair, always-valid methods, and direct inversion of nonnormal laws. Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) provide predictable-logging confidence sequences, Freidling, Zhao, and Gao (2026) study selection-conditioned randomization tests, and Cho, Bibaut, and Kallus (2025) invert simulated adaptive laws; none supplies this finite-population signed atomic calibration or joint common-void envelope. Chen et al. (2026) obtain a compound-Poisson HT law under independent Poisson importance sampling, while Hong, Leung, and Li (2020) treat limited overlap with diverging effective information. Shekhar and Ramdas (2023) prove i.i.d. bounded-mean width bounds rather than the present exact sequential two-sign tradeoff. Barbour and Xia (1999) support compound-Poisson error accounting, and Bhattacharjee and Goldstein (2019) identify the generalized Dickman constant-profile reduction. Liberali et al. (2025) remain the applied consumer, conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge for GUSTO-1 and EUROPA.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-transfer theorem couples the AIPW statistic, not the complete experiments, and therefore does not imply either all-estimator lower bound. The converse results instead use an exact common subprobability on a late-arm void event. The original constant-intensity frontier is optimized over residual geometry. The new joint frontier additionally optimizes deterministic intensity profiles but assumes honesty on the selected pair, because capped finite prefixes need not satisfy the declared profile contract for every \(n\). Its matching procedure knows the selected pair, so it establishes no global minimax attainment. Li and Zhao baseline-class honesty supplies the required pair honesty directly, transferring only the converse. The positive theorem still requires fixed profiles, deterministic domination for same-log threshold selection, and supplied profile and early-variation contracts. The \(0.442M\) high-hazard result remains a subfamily upper bound. The polynomial bit-complexity question remains open because no polynomial bound controls profile boxes that straddle the certification boundary.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Uniform finite-experiment coverage applies to the declared bounded Lipschitz intensity and signed-residual profile subclass with its supplied common profile event, early quadratic-variation envelope, and certified inputs. The original envelope \([(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+\) remains the constant-intensity, residual-optimized structured-class converse. The new joint envelope \([\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha]_+\) is proved under asymptotic honesty on each selected intensity-optimized two-sign pair and is optimized only within the deterministic late-void witness geometry. Exact attainment is pairwise only; no global minimax attainment is claimed. A direct inclusion argument transfers the joint converse, but neither attainment nor positive calibration, to Li and Zhao's baseline class. The original linear-ramp frontier, the exact \(1/8\) and \(0.60710678\) small-horizon-checked specialization, the directed \(13/32\) certificate, and the high-hazard \(0.442M\) radius remain valid. No polynomial certificate-complexity exponent is asserted. The Liberali et al. application is conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge; random-profile, Cox-process, and atom-free quantile extensions remain outside scope.
